Tidy coefficients from a fitted mlvar model

Source: R/mlvar.R
coefs.Rd

coefs() returns the temporal coefficients of a build_mlvar() fit as a data frame, one row per (outcome, predictor) pair: the fixed-effect lagged regression coefficients that make up the temporal network, with their standard errors and tests.

Only the within-person (temporal) coefficients are tabulated. The between-subjects effects that enter the between-subjects network through the D (I - Gamma) transformation are not given as a table of their own. The p-values are not adjusted for the number of coefficients, and significant is p < 0.05 for each coefficient on its own.

Usage

coefs(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_mlvar'
coefs(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
coefs(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A fitted model; only a net_mlvar from build_mlvar() has a method, and any other object raises an error.

...

Not used.

Value

A data frame with one row per (outcome, predictor) pair and the columns outcome (the variable predicted), predictor (the variable at the earlier occasion), beta (the fixed-effect coefficient), se (its standard error), t (beta / se), p (the two-sided p-value from the normal distribution, 2 * pnorm(-abs(t)), which stays above zero for large t), ci_lower and ci_upper (the 95% Wald interval, beta plus or minus qnorm(0.975) standard errors) and significant (p < 0.05).

Note

The idiographic package exports a function with the same name. With both packages attached, the one attached last masks the other; write Nestimate::coefs() to call this one.

Examples

# A three-variable ESM panel: 20 people x 20 beeps. `tired` is driven by
# `happy` one beep earlier, so the temporal network should recover it.
if (requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1)
  n_beep <- 20
  ar1 <- function(n, phi) as.numeric(stats::filter(stats::rnorm(n), phi,
                                                   method = "recursive"))
  panel <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(20), function(i) {
    happy <- ar1(n_beep, 0.4)
    data.frame(
      id    = i,
      beep  = seq_len(n_beep),
      happy = happy + stats::rnorm(1),
      calm  = ar1(n_beep, 0.3) + stats::rnorm(1),
      tired = 0.5 * c(0, happy[-n_beep]) + stats::rnorm(n_beep) +
              stats::rnorm(1)
    )
  }))
  fit <- build_mlvar(panel, vars = c("happy", "calm", "tired"),
                     id = "id", beep = "beep")
  fit
  coefs(fit)
  summary(fit)
}
